meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'kopecks / pennies' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: I haven't got a penny.

examples.text: Это стоит копейки.
examples.trans: It costs next to nothing.

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Сегодня не могу.
examples.trans: I can't today.

examples.text: Этого не может быть.
examples.trans: That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave (behind)', paired with 'оставлять'.

examples.text: Витя, можешь оставить эти деньги себе.
examples.trans: Vitya, you can keep this money for yourself.

examples.text: Я не оставлю его одного.
examples.trans: I won't leave him on his own.

examples.text: Оставь меня в покое!
examples.trans: Leave me alone!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'money' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Плевал он на ваши деньги.
examples.trans: He does not care about your money.

examples.text: Ни за какие деньги.
examples.trans: Not for any money.

examples.text: Ты же сама говорила, что это кровавые деньги.
examples.trans: You said yourself that it is blood money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to oneself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Уберите руки, что вы себе позволяете?
examples.trans: Take your hands off, what do you think you are doing?

examples.text: Я себя мужиком не чувствую.
examples.trans: I do not feel like a real man.

examples.text: Витя, можешь оставить эти деньги себе.
examples.trans: Vitya, you can keep this money for yourself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да там одна химия!
examples.trans: Why, there is nothing but chemicals in there!

examples.text: Там таких купюр много валяется.
examples.trans: There are plenty of banknotes like those lying around out there.

examples.text: Там всё нормально.
examples.trans: Everything's fine there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нельзя так, Витя!
examples.trans: You cannot do that, Vitya!

examples.text: Так твой папа нам блендер подарил.
examples.trans: Your dad just gave us a blender as a gift.

examples.text: Не думаю, что это просто так.
examples.trans: I do not think that is a coincidence.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'banknotes' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Там таких купюр много валяется.
examples.trans: There are plenty of banknotes like those lying around out there.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ладно, сейчас обед, немножко перекусите.
examples.trans: Fine, it is lunch now, have a little bite.

examples.text: Там таких купюр много валяется.
examples.trans: There are plenty of banknotes like those lying around out there.

examples.text: Мы сделали много.
examples.trans: We've done a lot.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is lying around'.

related.gloss: not to is lying around (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и валяться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and is lying around on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют валяться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to is lying around.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('prop / fake').

examples.text: Это бутафорские деньги.
examples.trans: This is prop money.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень бутафорский выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very prop choice.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hang in there'.

related.gloss: not to hang in there (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Держитесь меня, и всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Stick with me and everything will be fine.

examples.text: Держитесь меня, и всё у вас будет хорошо. Потому что я кто?
examples.trans: Stick with me, and everything will be fine for you. Because who am I?

examples.text: Надо держаться от неё подальше.
examples.trans: I need to stay further away from her.
